Pupils and teachers of Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola Primary School have been exposed to health risks following the accumulation of refuse directly in front of the school building along Shasha Road in the Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State. PUNCH Metro learnt that the refuse had remained uncleared for several weeks as the pupils and their teachers contended with the stench emanating from the decomposing waste. It was gathered that the offensive smell often spread into the school premises, making the learning environment uncomfortable. During a visit to the school on Friday, PUNCH Metro observed pupils covering their noses as they walked past the refuse heap during their arrival in the morning. Some of them were also seen trying to avoid the offensive smell as they made their way into the school premises. A similar sight was observed during the closing hour. A member of staff at the school, who spoke on condition of anonymity while citing privacy, said the situation had become increasingly uncomfortable, particularly for the pupils. “The smell is terrible, and it is difficult for us to pretend that everything is normal. The children inhale it every morning before getting into their classrooms, and the smell sometimes enters the school premises. “We have been experiencing this for over six months. It is not good for the children to be exposed to this kind of environment, especially when they are supposed to be in school to learn. We want the authorities to come and evacuate the refuse before it causes a health problem,” the staff member noted. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. She, however, questioned why the pupils should be made to endure such conditions in a learning environment. She said, “This is a very sad situation. Why should children be subjected to such an environment? The fact that this is a government-owned school should not mean that the pupils do not deserve a clean and healthy environment. “Every child deserves to learn in a decent environment. It is painful that these children have to contend with this kind of stench before they can even enter their school. The authorities should do something urgently.” Police bust Lagos cannabis farm, arrest Polish, Nigerian PHOTOS: Police uncover Lagos indoor cannabis farm, arrest two Meet Makoko scholars who defied odds to bag first class A resident of the area, who did not want his name in print, also expressed concern about the prolonged presence of the refuse heap. The resident said the situation had also become a source of discomfort for people living and doing business around the area. The resident said, “The refuse has been there for months. My question is, why should it be allowed to accumulate for this long in front of a school where children come to learn every day? The children have been enduring it. “The government should not wait until somebody falls sick before taking action. They should come and clear the refuse immediately.” Another resident, Kolapo Adekunle, said efforts to draw the attention of Private Sector Participation waste operators and officials of the Lagos Waste Management Authority to the refuse had not yielded any result. According to him, the operators regularly visited the community to evacuate waste but had repeatedly failed to clear the heap in front of the school. He said, “We have done all we could to bring the refuse to the attention of PSP operators and LAWMA, but nothing has been done about it. Of course, they come around to evacuate waste in this area. “Just about two weeks ago, we saw a LAWMA truck in front of the school, and we thought it was going to clear the refuse, but that did not happen. We were surprised that the waste was left there despite their presence.” Adekunle called on the relevant authorities to urgently evacuate the refuse. The spokesperson for LAWMA, Sanusi Olabamiji, could not be reached for comment, as calls made to his telephone line did not connect. A text message sent to him had yet to be replied to as of the time this report was filed. The situation at the school comes amid recurring waste management challenges across Lagos State, where residents in several communities have complained about delayed refuse evacuation and the re-emergence of heaps of garbage on roads, medians and residential streets.
